provenance.note: the wave ids are MACHINE fields so that a narrative may name a wave without the narrative inventing a number the artifact does not carry

purpose: Frontier option (D) from the Wf-A153 frontier scan: profile the METAL's coordination sphere (coordination number, neighbour element multiset, donor-class breakdown, rule-based oxidation state) for every row of the generation pool named in population.pool_path, and cross-tab it against the ligand-only connectivity to test whether a fragmented ligand leaves the metal under-coordinated.

population.pool_kind: post-hoc single decode of ONE checkpoint — NOT a training-set-distribution sampling

what_this_is_not.not_8_51_percent: This is NOT the end-to-end single-molecule rate published in metrics/by_metric/cfm_fragmentation_audit.json (/summary/generation_side/single_molecule_rate_end_to_end): a MEDIAN over 9 RUNS (its median RATE is carried verbatim in this artifact's end_to_end_headline.median field, read from that artifact at run time). A run-level end-to-end rate is over a DIFFERENT population (9 runs, not ONE pool of 2112 rows).
what_this_is_not.not_25_05_percent: This is NOT the 25.05 % SINGLE-FRAGMENT fraction of THIS pool (re-measured here, not quoted). A fragment count is not a coordination number: the coordination number is a per-atom property of the metal's neighbourhood. A row can be a single fragment AND hold a metal with an empty or an over-full sphere, so the two quantities are not a restatement of one another.
what_this_is_not.not_a_frontier_comparison: This is NOT comparable to the 92.7-94 % frontier band — see comparability_statement for the 4 independent breaks.
what_this_is_not.oxidation_state_is_inferred: The oxidation state is a RULE-BASED INFERENCE (three labelled layers), never a measurement. Only Layer B, and only inside its declared scope, is derived from the SMILES; Layer C is a repo PRIOR.

comparability_statement.summary: This metric is NOT comparable to the published 92.7-94 % frontier band, and no number in this artifact may be presented as comparable to it. 4 independent breaks separate the two.

breaks.frontier: the frontier band is over 10,000 unconditional QM9 samples, sampled from the training-set distribution.
breaks.ours: ours is ONE pool of 2112 rows from ONE post-hoc decode (pool directory: cfm_c8_fullgen_2026_10_24).

breaks.frontier: 'connected' in the frontier band means the DECODER's own connectivity claim; their 'Valid' means RDKit sanitisation and their '% PB-Valid' means PoseBusters geometry.
breaks.ours: here 'connected' means an RDKit fragment count of the emitted SMILES, and the coordination sphere is the metal's RDKit bond neighbourhood — a quantity the frontier band does not report at all. Neither frontier quantity is a coordination quantity.

breaks.frontier: the frontier publishes the post-processing axis in ONE table -- HLTF arXiv:2603.27113v1 Table 1(b) reports six models RAW and POST-PROCESSED side by side -- so 'the frontier number' is one of two numbers depending on the arm; the other frontier papers print a single arm. The published 92.7-94 % band's two endpoints are both RAW (post_processed: false); which frontier cells the band names is NOT settled on disk (COMPETING provenance readings, all in molmetal/reports/wfa158_frontier_postproc_matrix/frontier_matrix.json -- among them the readings listed at the JSON path `band_provenance`.`competing_reading_and_what_this_does_not_settle`.`readings` and the reading at the JSON path `sources`.`EF-TALFM` -- that do not even agree on the numerals), and the NUMBER of competing readings is itself NOT settled on disk. What holds under EVERY reading: the band is external, is NOT one homogeneous quantity, and is NOT on our scale.
breaks.ours: the pool measured here is RAW (no post-processing, no repair), so it is comparable only to a RAW frontier arm, never to a post-processed one.

breaks.frontier: the frontier's POST-PROCESSED arm adds explicit hydrogens; the raw arm's hydrogen convention is not stated by the record.
breaks.ours: this pool carries NO explicit H atom in any of its 2112 rows — measured here, not assumed — so it is measured with implicit H, which changes both sanitisation and geometry, and therefore the coordination count.

definitions.coordination_number: RDKit GetDegree() of the metal atom = the number of atoms covalently bonded to it. The pool's metals carry no implicit H (GetDegree() == GetTotalDegree() in every row), so the count is a heavy-atom neighbour count. The pool carries no dative ('->') bond, so every metal-incident bond is a covalent SINGLE or DOUBLE; a DOUBLE bond still contributes ONE neighbour (a metal-oxo is one donor).
definitions.coordination_sphere: the metal's RDKit bond neighbourhood — the atoms reachable in ONE bond from the metal WITHIN the metal's own fragment. A donor sitting in ANOTHER fragment of the same row is NOT in the sphere; it is counted separately as a disconnected_donor.
definitions.coordination_class: empty (CN 0) / under (CN < expected_cn) / at_capacity (CN == expected_cn) / over (CN > expected_cn), where expected_cn = coordination_capacity(metal, DEFAULT_OXIDATION_STATE[metal]) from molmetal.data.metal_smiles — the metal's USUAL oxidation state (the repo prior). The secondary classification coordination_class_os_derived instead uses the capacity implied by the structure-derived oxidation state.

oxidation_state_layers.os_formal_charge: Layer A — ionic-approximation identity. In a complex written in the IONIC convention the metal's formal charge in the SMILES IS its oxidation state, because every ligand's ionic charge already sits on the ligand. OS_A(M) = q(M). Under the COVALENT convention (every atom written neutral) this returns 0, which is NOT evidence of a metal(0) centre — it is the ABSENCE of charge information. ASSUMED RULE, not a measurement of the oxidation state.
oxidation_state_layers.os_charge_balanced: Layer B — ionic-approximation with a MONATOMIC-X scope. OS_B(M) = Q_row + sum(donor contributions), where Q_row is the total formal charge of the row's molecule and each donor contributes the negation of its LIGAND's oxidation state: a monatomic halide donor (X-type) contributes +1 (OS = -1), a neutral L-type donor (amine / pyridine / water / phosphine) contributes 0, and an anionic donor carrying formal charge -1 that is the ONLY charged atom in the metal's fragment contributes +1 (a monatomic anionic X-type ligand, OS = -1). This is exact for the classic covalent-written cis-[M(NH3)2X2] case (two halides -> +2) and for a metal carbanion. It is OUT OF SCOPE for any row whose metal's fragment holds a charged atom that is not one of those monatomic anionic donors (e.g. a carboxylate written [O-], whose ligand oxidation state is NOT the sum of its atoms' formal charges) — such a row reports os_charge_balanced = null rather than a number. When the computed value is not positive it is reported but NOT usable as an oxidation state (os_charge_balanced_usable = false). ASSUMED RULE, not a measurement.
oxidation_state_layers.os_prior_default: Layer C — the repo's own DEFAULT oxidation state per metal, copied verbatim from molmetal/scripts/train_cfm_yuelbond_wasserstein.py:11399 (_DEFAULT_OXIDATION_STATE). A PRIOR chosen by the repo; NOT derived from any SMILES and NOT a measurement. Used only as the fallback when Layers A and B are silent.

population.n_frags_column_mismatch_note: rows where the pool's n_frags_raw column differs from the RDKit fragment count re-measured here

coordination_number.definition: RDKit GetDegree() of the metal atom: the number of atoms covalently bonded to it (heavy-atom neighbours; the pool's metals carry no implicit H, so GetDegree() == GetTotalDegree() in every row).
coordination_number.empty_sphere_note: the empty-sphere rows are the metal-ALONE rows; the excluding-empty statistics are reported next to the all-rows ones so neither is silently dropped

coordination_class.definition: empty = CN 0; under/at_capacity/over compare the measured CN against expected_cn = coordination_capacity(metal, DEFAULT_OXIDATION_STATE[metal]) — the metal's USUAL oxidation state, i.e. the repo PRIOR. The metal is over-coordinated when CN > expected. This is the PRIMARY classification; the structure-derived-OS variant is under coordination_class_secondary_os_derived.

coordination_class_secondary_os_derived.definition: the SAME classification but against the capacity implied by the STRUCTURE-DERIVED oxidation state (Layer B) where it is in scope, and by the prior otherwise. This is a SECONDARY check and is reported separately because Layer B can UNDER-estimate the metal's true oxidation state: a complex with exactly ONE X-type (halide) donor and five neutral donors yields OS = +1, whose capacity is smaller than the metal's real one, so an octahedral Ir(III)/Rh(III) centre is spuriously flagged over-coordinated. The PRIMARY check uses the metal's USUAL oxidation state (the repo prior).

donor_classes.definition: the element class of each atom covalently bonded to the metal: N_donor / O_donor / C_donor / halide / S_donor / P_donor / Se_donor / other

donor_motif_distribution.definition: the sorted multiset of the metal's neighbour elements, e.g. 'N,N,N,Cl'; this is the coordination motif

geometry_class.definition: molmetal.data.coord_geometry.classify_coord_geometry(CN, Z, DEFAULT_OXIDATION_STATE[metal]) — the geometry class implied by the measured CN under the metal's USUAL oxidation state (the repo prior)

metal_alone_in_fragment.definition: rows whose metal has NO bonded neighbour, i.e. the metal is alone in its own RDKit fragment. The coordination sphere is EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION for these rows — they are reported separately and never averaged away.

finding_1_no_metal_is_over_coordinated.statement: NO metal in the pool is over-coordinated relative to its usual oxidation state's coordination capacity. Every departure is UNDER-coordination or an EMPTY sphere.

finding_2_the_oxidation_state_is_not_in_.statement: Every metal atom and every donor atom in the pool is written with formal charge 0, so the emitted SMILES carries NO oxidation-state information at all. The oxidation state used for the capacity check is therefore a PRIOR for most rows, and even the structure-derived Layer B can only fire on the rows that carry a halide donor.

finding_3_fragmentation_does_NOT_signifi.statement: HONEST NEGATIVE. The binary cross-tab does NOT support the 'a fragmented ligand leaves the metal under-coordinated' story: the under-or-empty rate is statistically indistinguishable between single-fragment and fragmented rows. The continuous correlations are WEAK (|r| <= 0.0878). Fragmentation and coordination loss are largely INDEPENDENT in this pool.

finding_4_the_donor_split_mechanism_is_R.statement: HONEST NEGATIVE. For most fragmented, under-coordinated rows the donors were NOT split off: the missing coordination is fully covered by split-off donors in only 93 of 451 rows (20.62 %). A split-off donor is therefore NOT a general explanation of the fragmentation.

finding_5_the_metal_alone_rows_ARE_the_d.statement: The 30 metal-ALONE rows are the one case where the donor split mechanism holds outright: every one of them has at least one donor atom sitting in another fragment, and they carry the highest disconnected-donor counts of any coordination class. Their coordination sphere is EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a modelling failure.

finding_6_the_donor_sets_are_CARBON_DOMI.statement: The emitted coordination spheres are dominated by CARBON donors, not by the classical N/O/halide donor sets of the Pt(II)/Ru(II)/Ir(III) metallodrug literature. That is a property of the emitted SMILES, and it is a chemistry observation, not a defect verdict.

findings_note: the six finding KEYS are legacy schema labels from Wf-A155 and are kept for compatibility; what THIS run found is in each finding's 'verdict' field and in its 'statement'

cross_tab_fragmentation_vs_coordination.question: does a fragmented ligand correlate with an under- or an over-coordinated metal?

fragmented_vs_single_fragment.definition: fragmented = row_n_frags > 1; single = row_n_frags == 1. 'under_or_empty' = measured CN < expected_cn (the empty sphere counted as under-coordinated, since an empty sphere is the limiting case of a lost donor).

cross_tab_fragmentation_vs_coordination.pearson_note: p-values use a normal approximation to the t distribution; this run has n = 2112 metal atoms, so the approximation is accurate (n is in the thousands).

candidate_mechanism.hypothesis: A fragmented ligand leaves the metal under-coordinated because its donor atoms were split into separate fragments, leaving the metal's own fragment with too few neighbours.
candidate_mechanism.test: count donor-type atoms (N/O/S/P/Se/halide) that are DISCONNECTED from the metal, i.e. sitting in another fragment of the same row

donor_split_fully_explains_the_missing_c.definition: rows whose (expected_cn - measured CN) missing neighbours are covered by at least that many donor atoms found disconnected from the metal in the same row

counter_evidence.note: donors split off also occur in rows whose metal is already at capacity, so a split donor is not by itself evidence of the fragmentation cause

per_row_sphere.format: columnar: one list per metal atom, fields in the order given by per_row_columns. row_index is the index into the pool CSV's data rows (0-based, header excluded).

narrative_self_consistency.rule: every number rendered in a narrative string must be backed by a machine field of the same artifact -- as a standalone number inside a machine string, or equal (to the token's own decimal count) to a machine number
